Shahbag.question: On 27 March 1971, _____ destroyed the Kali temple and its 120 feet tower
Shahbag.fact: On 27 March 1971, Pakistani Army destroyed the Kali temple and its 120 feet tower. The hotel, which had been declared a neutral zone, nonetheless came under fire from both combatants in the war—the Mukti Bahini and Pakistani army.

Shahbag.question: In 1912, _____ convened here again under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah, and met with Lord Hardinge, the Viceroy of India
Shahbag.fact: Originally, a dance-hall for the performances of Baijees, or dancing women, (including, among the famous ones, Piyari Bai, Heera Bai, Wamu Bai and Abedi Bai), the mansion became the venue for the All-India Muslim Education Society Conference in 1906, which was attended by 4,000 participants. In 1912, Society convened here again under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah, and met with Lord Hardinge, the Viceroy of India.

Shahbag.question: In 1971 the _____ of Kali was destroyed by the Pakistani Army in the Liberation War of Bangladesh
Shahbag.fact: In the late 1920s, Sri Anandamoyi Ma, the noted Hindu ascetic, also called the Mother of Shahbagh, built her ashram near Ramna Kali Mandir, or the Temple of Kali, at Ramna. In 1971 the Temple of Kali was destroyed by the Pakistani Army in the Liberation War of Bangladesh.

Shahbag.question: The Basanta Utsab (_____ of Spring) takes place every 14 February—the first day of spring, according to the reformed Bangladeshi calendar
Shahbag.fact: The Basanta Utsab (Festival of Spring) takes place every 14 February—the first day of spring, according to the reformed Bangladeshi calendar. Basanta Utsab has become a major festival in Dhaka since it was first celebrated in Shahbagh in the 1960s.
